module_title: The Revolt of 1857 - Nature, Consequences, and Historiography
introduction: This advanced level analyzes the profound aftermath of the revolt, including the structural changes introduced by the Government of India Act 1858, military reorganization, and the diverse perspectives of historians regarding the true nature of the uprising.

core_concepts.title: Government of India Act 1858
core_concepts.description: As a direct consequence of the revolt, the rule of the East India Company was abolished. The administration of India was transferred directly to the British Crown (Queen Victoria).

core_concepts.title: Creation of the Viceroy Post
core_concepts.description: The title of Governor-General was changed to 'Viceroy' (the personal representative of the Crown). Lord Canning became the last Governor-General and the first Viceroy of India.

core_concepts.title: Military Reorganization (Peel Commission)
core_concepts.description: The Peel Commission was appointed to reorganize the army. The ratio of European to Indian soldiers was increased (1:2 in Bengal, 1:3 in Madras/Bombay), and artillery was kept strictly in European hands.

core_concepts.title: Historiography (Nature of the Revolt)
core_concepts.description: V.D. Savarkar called it the 'First War of Independence'. Conversely, R.C. Majumdar stated it was 'neither first, nor national, nor a war of independence'. T.R. Holmes described it as a 'conflict between civilization and barbarism'.

core_concepts.title: The Queen's Proclamation
core_concepts.description: Read by Lord Canning at Minto Park in Allahabad on November 1, 1858, it promised to abandon the policy of territorial extension (annexation) and pledged religious non-interference.

important_entities.name: V.D. Savarkar
important_entities.significance: Authored the book 'The Indian War of Independence, 1857', giving the revolt a strongly nationalist interpretation.

important_entities.name: S.N. Sen
important_entities.key_fact: Official Historian of the Government of India
important_entities.significance: Commissioned by the Indian government to write the official history of the revolt. His book is titled 'Eighteen Fifty Seven'.

important_entities.name: R.C. Majumdar
important_entities.significance: In his book 'The Sepoy Mutiny and the Rebellion of 1857', he critically dismissed the idea that it was a cohesive national struggle.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often confuse R.C. Majumdar with the official historian. Majumdar was initially approached but left due to disagreements. 'S.N. Sen' is the correct official historian.
The Queen's Proclamation of 1858 was read in 'Allahabad' (Prayagraj), not in Delhi or Calcutta, which were traditional power centers.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember that the 'Peel' Commission was meant to consolidate British military power and reorganize the army after the mutiny.

exam_strategy_tips: Pay close attention to quotes by different historians and British officials; identifying who said what about the nature of the revolt is a favorite for UPSC/State PSCs.
Understand the administrative shifts brought by the 1858 Act, especially the creation of the office of the 'Secretary of State for India'.
